<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a VCS package for xdm-app-git that builds from the master branch of the upstream Git repository (https://github.com/subhra74/xdm). It follows standard AUR packaging practices for git-based packages, including versioning based on git describe and skipping SHA-256 checksums for the Git source, which is normal and expected behavior.

The package downloads a prebuilt JetBrains Runtime (JBR) SDK for build-time use only. This is clearly documented in the comments: the JBR is required because the build system (packaging/build-bundle.sh) explicitly checks for a specific version (jbr.version=25.0.4.1, jbr.build=b635.70), and the native Wayland support in XDM depends on JetBrains-specific patches not present in upstream OpenJDK. The JBR tarballs are fetched from JetBrains' official cache-redirector and verified using hard-coded SHA-512 checksums matching those published by JetBrains. This is a legitimate and secure method for including a required build dependency.

The build process uses Maven with a locally defined toolchain pointing to the verified JBR, builds a fat JAR, and then creates an app image using packaging/build-bundle.sh. All build artifacts are created under $srcdir, avoiding interference with the user's home directory (e.g., ~/.m2). The resulting binary is installed under /opt/xdm-app with appropriate symlinks and desktop integration.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or suspicious file operations. The package conflicts with other XDM variants to prevent file conflicts, and provides clean integration with the system. While the use of a prebuilt JBR might raise hygiene concerns, it is justified by technical requirements and securely implemented with proper checksum verification. This does not constitute a supply-chain attack.
</details>
